summary: The design, spec, config handling and lifecycle code substantially follow the directive. Model and auto_approve are configuration values with fail-closed validation. The review gate is a native external gate with category 'review'. Findings route to the worker inbox, revisions supersede gates, attempt exhaustion, explicit escalation or auto_approve=false create an operator approval blocker, and a pass waits for a manager-signed BIP340 receipt before resolution and group posting. Unit tests cover spawn, findings, revise, pass/escalate, forged receipts, drift, runner failure and malformed results. The artifact cannot pass for four reasons. The end-to-end acceptance criterion (one real bead review against Fuel iX opus) has no evidence, even though btq-c2p is closed. No test execution results are supplied. The retained decision evidence records only the configured model, not the resolved model the design requires. The dispatcher can wedge a workstream's review concurrency slot on a stale pending job. One further risk, not treated as blocking and not verifiable from this evidence: with the default config and no explicit provider, review_runner derives requested provider 'fuelix' from the model string, which may not resolve in Hermes without provider=custom and base_url set.
blocking_findings: Acceptance criterion 'end-to-end: one real bead review against fuelix opus once btq-c2p lands' is unmet or unevidenced. btq-c2p is closed, but the supplied artifacts contain no retained real-model run: no docs/evidence/btq-ejp/ contents, reviewer session, model identity, evidence hash, verified signed receipt or group delivery message IDs. docs/review-gate.md itself lists this as required validation.

No test execution evidence is supplied for tests/test_review_gate.py or the full harness regression suite, which the design names as the regression gate. The lifecycle tests exist, but they are not shown passing.

The design requires decision evidence to carry both the 'configured and resolved model'. review_runner.main sets result['model'] = settings['model'], which is the configured string only. The runtime provider, base_url and model actually used by AIAgent are never captured in result.json, the appraisal or the signed receipt, so the group-posted record cannot prove which model performed the review.

review_dispatch.artifact_tick calls review_gate.current() for every pending, running or reviewed artifact job. On any failure (scope, policy, ownership or artifact drift, or the task leaving in_progress) it records an error and returns True, and tick() stops at the first artifact job that returns True. A stale pending job is never marked stale or superseded, so it permanently blocks every later model launch for the workstream, including legacy progress/completion reviews. The legacy path marks scope-changed jobs 'stale'; the artifact path should do the same for non-running jobs, and add a test for stale pending jobs. The design lists stale task/artifact/policy as required coverage.

Artifact job launch in artifact_tick bypasses reviews.held(store, run), which the legacy path checks before start(). The shared concurrency and hold guard that the spec claims is shared is therefore only partially shared.
